gloss: lectern; podium; platform (for speaking or lecturing)

definitions.gloss: lectern; podium; platform (for speaking or lecturing)
definitions.explanation: lectern; podium; platform (for speaking or lecturing)

examples.japanese: {教授|きょうじゅ}が{講壇|こうだん}に{立|た}った。
examples.english: The professor stood at the lectern.

examples.japanese: {講壇|こうだん}から{学生|がくせい}たちに{語|かた}りかけた。
examples.english: He addressed the students from the podium.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{長年|ながねん}{大学|だいがく}の{講壇|こうだん}に{立|た}ち、{多|おお}くの{学生|がくせい}を{育|そだ}ててきた。
examples.english: He stood at the university lectern for many years and trained many students.

notes:
Refers to the raised platform or lectern from which a lecturer speaks. Can also refer figuratively to the position or role of being a lecturer or academic.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {講壇|こうだん}に{立|た}つ: to stand at the lectern; to take the podium
- {講壇|こうだん}から{降|お}りる: to step down from the podium
- {大学|だいがく}の{講壇|こうだん}: the university lectern (i.e., an academic position)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {演壇|えんだん}: podium, rostrum — used for speeches and presentations, not limited to academic settings
- {教壇|きょうだん}: teaching platform — the raised area at the front of a classroom; emphasizes the teaching role
- {壇上|だんじょう}: on the stage/platform — refers to the space itself rather than the structure
